text.p: These are the leading stories in Malawi's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Malawi President Bakili Muluzi who on Monday paid a surprise visit to some Blantyre primary schools warned moonlighting teachers that he would fire them if they were caught attending to private classes at the expense of the pupils they were employed for in government schools.

- Malawi's sixth university college, expected to open in 1998 starting with the faculty of education in Mzuzu, the country's northern region will also offer distance courses, Education Minister Brown Mpinganjira said on Monday.

- Main opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) President Gwanda Chakuamba appealed to party supporters to strongly rally behind it to eject the ruling United Democratic Front (UDF) party in the 1999 general elections.
